key_concepts: Gravity is a force of attraction between all objects with mass
Gravitational pull strength depends on mass and distance
Earth's gravity pulls objects downward and keeps them from floating away
The Sun's gravity keeps Earth in orbit at a life-supporting distance
The Moon's gravity causes ocean tides
Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is measured in grams or kilograms
Weight is the gravitational force on an object's mass and is measured in newtons
Heavier and lighter objects fall at the same rate when air resistance is negligible
Air resistance affects falling motion and can slow objects such as feathers or flat paper
In a vacuum, a feather and a baseball fall at the same rate
Terminal velocity occurs when air resistance equals the force of gravity
